answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a tundra, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 81 aliases therefore burns 334 bonds held for 19 days each, plus the walnut attestations those aliases can never earn. A single mesa checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
